contract: One recorded pure pattern cycle and ordinary dispatcher per host Unit/Run: shared sealed request charge, the binding of each action chosen by its action kind and, for a schema map, its schema ID, schema/identity/committed host gate/Budget/authority/Approval checks, occurrence-first settlement, a nested callable's first admitted finish given to its parent once each child cost is known or final unknown (the committed child amount when all are known, no actual when one is final unknown), a nested_callable slot that settles closing its child callable and every callable below it in the same fold step (closed, without state, so their state bounds leave control; their open slots settle by their own rules and child costs still reach the parent Budget), a change of Attempt settling every open slot of the older Attempt in the same fold step (refused with actual 0 when nothing can have been sent, `unknown` with the reservation held when something may have been sent, running local work `local_closed`), so no older-Attempt slot stays open, the end of a Run settling, by the same closer with reason `run_closed`, every open slot that the request-cap stop does not retain before its deadline, at the terminal view and at each later protocol input, so a terminal Run keeps no other slot open, durable owner composition and explicit fail-stop recovery; charge exhaustion stops generation while retaining prior within-cap obligations, without new work or resend permission; `input/4`, `control/4` and `status/1` each wait for the engine at most 60,000 ms; optional read-only result/3 returns the first accepted completed source outcome after exact Run and evidence cross-checks within shared finite history budgets (65,536 rows, 536,870,912 canonical bytes, and 16,777,216 bytes per record). Native v2 is opt-in with protocol_version: 2 and a fresh fixed-version Unit; omitted/1 retains v1 state, fingerprint and behavior. The v2 event source is fixed by ID/version and receives exact tenant/principal/run_id scope. wait_event supports zero-estimate admission through Budget public :status with reservation:nil; positive waits reserve and release, and other actions/versions retain existing reservation behavior. Read-only event_waits folds and verifies retained history with exact scope, DTO, limits and errors documented in README. Read-only transcript/3 returns one Run's committed history in commit order (inputs, gate and authorization verdicts, admitted actions with their callable path, nested starts and kept finishes, settlements with their record kind, reason and actual, later actuals and the terminal outcome), each entry derived from the folded state change of one committed record with its own recorded time, with the call path, scope, limits, reader configuration, reading, budgets, rechecks and errors of event_waits; it calls no callback, mutates nothing and emits no telemetry.
limits: Host provides authenticated correlation/current authority, checked pure prompt patterns/bindings/schemas (for each schema map a binding for every action schema that a pattern of the Run asks for under that kind, whose `result` is the schema that the pattern reads; each action schema in `schemas`; the same `bindings` on each restart), exclusive matching Store/Lease construction, ordinary supervision, clocks/wakes, capacity, outcome sink and physical fencing/outstanding-write confirmation before recovery. Byte caps are not a sandbox.

No model/tool/Lua dependency, recipe loader, child Run, cluster ownership, scheduler, hot configuration, implicit reopen, retry/rearm/reset or later-wave capability. One Run stream belongs exclusively to RunApprovalRelease; old Run remains unchanged.

Payload JSON <=65536 bytes/depth32; ingress <=262144; complete record/output <=16777216; control <=2097152 with future settlement/receipt reservations and the whole state bound of each open callable (the root 65536; a nested child the state_bytes of its nested binding, 1 to 65536, else 65536); slot <=131072, 64 active/256 lifetime occurrences; request map <=4456448; checkpoint <=33554432 including model, retained IDs, full replay witnesses and framing. Complete encoded bounds are authoritative; no truncation or borrowed future settlement capacity. An input that settles no slot is given to a pattern only when control has room for its invocation entry; with no room it is classified `record_size` and no invocation entry, no pattern call, no charge, no receipt and no request is kept.

A binding is chosen by action kind and, for a schema map entry, by `schema_id` alone: two versions of one schema ID under one kind share one binding, a schema map has no default entry so an unmapped schema is refused as `missing_binding`, and bindings are fixed for the Run so a changed schema map is an incompatible restart. A nested child still finishes with the `result` of the binding chosen for its parent's action; a wrapper for another child schema belongs to the host. A `local_work` binding gives its `result` at version 1.

A nested finish reaches the parent only when its `{schema_id, schema_version}` equals the binding `result`, else the parent fails as `nested_result_invalid`; no finish keeps `nested_completed`. Only the first admitted finish counts; the payload is recipe content within the payload bounds, uninterpreted and not in `status/1`; it is dropped from durable control state once the parent action settles. That first finish is admitted only when control with it placed in it still satisfies the bound: its bytes are held in the reserve from admission until the continuation keeps it, and with no room it is refused `record_size` (the child gets an ordinary refusal, stays open, and its parent stays open). A final unknown child cost (a settled action whose Budget entry is still held, with no actual and no later record that can give one) gives the parent no actual; its share and the child entries stay held until each action's deadline, then the Budget's expiry stops counting them, and nothing is committed or released as zero; no later reconciliation of a lost cost exists. A parent of an older Attempt is settled at the change of Attempt; a parent of a terminal Run is handed an outcome only when the request-cap stop retains it and its deadline has not passed; after the deadline it is not selected and the next protocol input of the current Attempt settles it with the end of the Run. A nested start is kept only when control has room for the state bound of the child, its Budget and its authority; with no room the parent action is refused record_size with actual 0 and nothing dispatched, and no child exists. A pattern state over the bound of its callable is not stored. The state of a callable leaves control when the callable closes, and its room comes back; when the slot of a nested_callable settles, its child callable and every callable below it close in the same fold step, so a child whose parent settled while it was open keeps neither its state nor its reserve, and its slots settle by their own rules.

A Run recorded before the change-of-Attempt repair, with a change of Attempt and open slots, folds to another state after it (Elzoo is not released). The settlement at a change is part of the run_view fold step: it writes no protocol record, and the reason `attempt_closed` is in the outcome given to the request tracker and the join, not in a separate journal record. A Run recorded before the repair of the over-cap deny that already holds such a slot (a settled parent that an over-cap deny turned back to refusing) keeps it until a change of Attempt sets it settled again with its first settlement untouched; Elzoo is not released. Rows that a test cannot hold (a running child finish; ready for local work, ask_person, nested callable and finish) are covered by the code path only.

A child that never sends a finish that fits leaves its parent action waiting. Three rules settle that parent: its deadline, when an input of the current Attempt reaches the engine at or after it while the Run is not terminal (the engine has no timer for the deadline of a slot), a change of Attempt, and the end of the Run with the other open slots (run_closed).

A Run recorded before the repair of the end of the Run, with a terminal view and open slots, folds to another state after it (Elzoo is not released). The settlement is part of the fold step and writes no protocol record; the reason run_closed is in the outcome given to the request tracker and the join, and neither keeps it, so no state shows it and no test asserts it. It is less exact than the drain was, on the safe side: a Resource slot in ready and a model or tool slot in approval with a request key are settled unknown with the reservation held, also when the Run lists no Effect for it, and a refusal that was decided but not recorded loses its own reason and class. The engine has no timer: a retained slot past its deadline stays open until the next protocol input of the current Attempt. No test of the end of the Run holds a slot in approval with a request key, ready with an approved request key, a ready Resource slot, a refusing nested parent with a child or a running child finish: the code path only.

A Run recorded before the repair of the room of a child finish, with a finish that was admitted and not yet kept, can meet the refusal `record_size` on replay where the old code had none (Elzoo is not released).

A Run recorded before the repair of the state bound can fold to another state: a larger reserve can refuse a nested start or a request that fitted, and the state of a closed callable is gone (Elzoo is not released). The last bytes of the control bound are not reserved for small growth: a refusal adds its reason to its slot (a slot within a few bytes of its bound of 131072 can pass it), and the refusal of a nested start makes control 2 bytes larger only when the expiry of the parent is below 256 ms (the released Budget entry is 15 bytes, the open one 13 bytes for an expiry up to 255 and at least 16 above), so it can pass the bound only when control is within 2 bytes of it.

A reply of the Run to an approval request that is not ok and leaves no listed request is waited for when it is a conflict, unavailable or indeterminate: each drain then ends at that slot, and a slot whose Run never answers stays open until its deadline or a change of Attempt. A Run recorded before this repair that already holds the false refusal approval_refused keeps it (Elzoo is not released).

A Run recorded before the repair of the invocation entries can fold to another state: an input that settles no slot and has no room is refused where the old engine called the pattern (Elzoo is not released).

Request cap 1..256 is sealed per Run, shared with nested callables and never replenished by Attempt, pause/continue or restart. First excess creates only charge/stop bookkeeping, not actions/verdicts/outcomes/joins or a pattern input. Room rollover is explicit after prior terminal obligations settle; lifetime-action capacity is not reset.

`input/4`, `control/4` and `status/1` use one fixed call limit of 60,000 ms and take no limit operand or option; `status/1` replies only after an input that the engine is working on. An input at the bounds (64 active/256 lifetime actions) took about 4.2 to 5.0 s in 10 runs alone and 10 beside the Piece suite on a shared worker host, mostly in the journal write path of the owners below this Piece: one observation, not a time bound. A caller that needs a shorter wait runs the call in a process of its own and gives up the wait there (`Task.async/1`, `Task.yield/2`, `Task.shutdown/2`). When a call ends by the limit or its caller stops waiting, the exit says nothing about whether the input was applied and the engine goes on with it; the Contract states only the existing retry rule (the same ID again, never another; applied/duplicate means committed; changed bytes are a conflict) and no other way to learn the outcome or bound on the continued work.

FIFO DU input retention does not bound retained log/witness memory or recovery time. Full retained history is required for audit; pruned/damaged/incompatible history errors. Oversize checkpoint refuses nonfatally; no perpetual checkpoint guarantee.

Finite disposable-PostgreSQL/counting-fake-provider evidence, not production monitoring, universal proof, exactly-once external effects or physical no-send/cancellation. Unknown cost is not zero; Budget estimates do not enforce provider charges. Reserved intents/lost raw sink values never authorize resend.

Read-only result/3 requires an exact trusted tenant/principal/run scope and exact max_records/max_bytes limits (1..65,536 rows; 1..536,870,912 canonical bytes). Unit and completion-evidence rows share both budgets, the 16,777,216-byte per-record cap applies, and the host supplies fully retained history with truthful committed-append visibility; noncompleted Runs expose no payload and result reads invoke no callback or mutation.

Native v2 outside-event waits require an exact fixed source descriptor and corroborated retained history; event IDs use nonempty UTF-8 and native ingress bounds, not the source descriptor ID limit. event_waits requires exact scope keys and exact positive max_records/max_bytes operands, capped at 65,536 records and 536,870,912 bytes; it returns at most 64 * request_cap waits and the documented bounded reader errors.

A transcript is the committed history of a running engine, not an audit record, metric, trace export or cache, and it emits no telemetry. Outcome payloads other than admitted action payloads are not shown. The host must supply full retained history; a pruned history is refused, not summarized. Reading a Run whose engine is not running is not covered.

listed finite scenarios, not quantified proofs.; read-only result/3 acceptance covers native local and nested completion, Memory and PostgreSQL evidence, scope-before-I/O, budgets, damaged history, unavailable reads, first-settlement selection, restart and repeated-read invariance The `native outbox acknowledgement reconciliation` group contains the tests `confirms the original canonical identity after committed reply loss and reopens a completed result`, `keeps noncommitted and unreadable acknowledgements halted without another offer or charge`, and `does not treat a different winning nonce as confirmation of the original ack`: a real PostgreSQL ack runs before its reply is hidden and is confirmed with the original key/nonce through public DurableLog.confirm_ack/2; rollback, unavailable confirmation reads and a superseding nonce remain explicitly unknown, repeated halted offers add no work or Budget charge, and the completed-cut reopen preserves Run, Attempt, Unit, result, work, Budget and outbox state. The `keeps malformed confirmation evidence unknown after a committed acknowledgement` test corrupts the stored ack digest after a real PostgreSQL commit and observes public confirmation remain unknown, with the engine halted and no fresh acknowledgement, work, Budget or outbox mutation. The finite fixture does not establish universal process/network cancellation or volatile-work recovery.
Pinned GenServer serialization, Registry/DynamicSupervisor and Task semantics compose ready owner Contracts; no local OTP runtime proof.
OTP29.1.2 deterministic minor-version-2 ETF/safe decoding and SHA-256 identities; full encoded bounds are checked, not inferred from JSON length.
Pinned compact JSON encoding/decoding retains admitted requests and originals; ready PayloadSchema owns JSON representation/depth/schema checks.

Host callbacks are prompt pure checked decisions where required, retain stable compatible identity/binding/schema bytes, authenticate people/results/current authority, serialize Run mutation with admission, preserve full durable history and fence old tasks/owners/providers. Native v2 also needs a truthful append-only source with stable identity/version, scope-consistent head/read and complete retained history; callbacks do not authenticate a production source. Fake observations and local PostgreSQL tests do not establish production fencing or vendor behavior. Reused Cure laws retain only their dependency-local scopes; no new engine proof or monitor is claimed.

Exercises native v2 state and action compatibility, zero-estimate wait admission with reservation:nil, positive post-event local-work charging, and refusal of zero estimates outside the supported v2 wait path.
Exercises source-correlated activation and event ingress, exact scope and source failures, replay and fenced recovery, stale cursor refusal, long event IDs, and ingress/paused-size boundaries.
Exercises bounded read-only event-wait history projection, scope/limits/errors, selected-version and source-identity recovery, no-callback behavior, and exact activation/input/result receipt pairing.

The eleven groups nested_tree, ask_paused, unknown_and_attempt_closed, later_actual, expired_before_its_own_outcome, outside_event_wait, gate_denial, earlier_run, scope_limits_reader, read_bounds and read_only exercise the read-only transcript: a completed two-level nested Run gives each path, nested start and kept finish, settlement with its record kind, the root finish with actual 0 and the terminal entry in commit order with the test clock's times; an ASK Run gives the ask verdict with its policy and no settlement; an Effect made unknown by a restart settles unknown with actual :unknown and a change of Attempt closes its slots by :run_view with no reason; a nested parent settled expired with no actual gets an :actual entry from the later nested_actual record; local work whose timeout outcome is committed after its deadline settles expired with no reason; a native v2 wait gives its action, outside-event input and settlement; a gate denial gives the deny verdict and its refusal reason with no action entry, and an engine refusal committed after another slot's deadline settles both in one record with a reason only for the refused slot; a Unit holding an earlier Run and a late input of it gives only the scoped Run; wrong scope, malformed limits and no reader fail with no Run-owner or Store read; exact limits succeed, one record or byte less is read_limit, an unavailable Store is unavailable and pruned history is history; and Unit, Run-owner and evidence heads and the gate, clock, binding and pattern counters are unchanged across two equal reads, with disposable PostgreSQL and the in-memory Store. A path without the link to its enclosing parent (nested_tree fails), entries from sequence 1 regardless of the configured Run (earlier_run fails), the configure check kept without filtering a protocol record of another Run (earlier_run fails), no :actual entry (later_actual fails) and the reason taken without the own-effect check (expired_before_its_own_outcome fails) are temporary negative controls; listed finite scenarios, not proofs.

telemetry.contract: OTP diagnostics only with redacted engine format_status; no custom telemetry, payload exporter or durable audit through observations.

config.contract: Fixed required host infrastructure, checked pattern/schema/gate/action bindings, explicit Run/period, request cap, monetary Budget, lifecycle rule/deadline and evidence Writer; compatible restart only, no defaults or hot replacement; optional exact result_reader %{evidence_store, retention_count} enables bounded read-only result/3, event_waits and transcript; optional protocol_version 2 requires an exact event_source descriptor and fingerprints its ID/version; source identity/version cannot change on recovery

control.contract: Trusted stable-ID input and begin-Attempt/Approval evidence-revocation/pause/verified continue/targeted cancel through existing owners; committed status and explicit host recovery, no generic router/reset/rearm or physical cancellation promise. Native v2 outside-event settlement is source-correlated and replays through the original input identity.
